deepdive.sec: Financials / Public Sector Bank — RAM-led balance-sheet re-mix & digital catch-up

bull_bear.body:
- **CRAR 17.61%** — comfortable; no capital raise discussed.
- **ECL pre-provisioning is the deliberate use of current earnings**: ~₹150cr this quarter, "more than what is currently required so that at the end when it kicks in on 1st April, we are in a better position." Framed as fundamentally strengthening the balance sheet; PCR rose to 92.33% as a result.
- **Portfolio rebalancing** is the main capital-allocation action: exit ₹5,000cr of low-yield exposure, redeploy into RAM.
- Net-worth build of ₹555cr in the quarter: ₹331cr profit + ₹170cr AFS reserve + ₹54cr DTA adjustment.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
1. **Sequential growth is weak** — total business +1.05%, credit +1.25%, deposits +0.89% QoQ, against peers reporting strong Q1 credit growth. Management's defence (Q1 is always subdued; growth is deliberately paced; the ₹5,000cr shedding depressed the optics) is plausible but needs a Q2 print to confirm.
2. **MSME slippages ticked up** and management expects "this run rate may continue," attributing it to global trickle-down effects. Not alarming to them; collection efficiency and SMA are improving.
3. **ECL transition (1-April)** — the size of the eventual requirement is not disclosed; the <1% credit-cost guidance is a buffer, not a computed number.
4. **Two state-government-guaranteed accounts fluctuate in and out of SMA 1/2** — currently out, but a recurring lumpy distorter of the SMA series.
5. **Treasury dependence and rate risk** — G-sec at 6.8% heading to 6.90%; crude ~$90; Gulf turmoil unresolved. Last year's Q1 operating profit leaned on ~₹200cr of treasury.
6. **Structurally high cost-to-income (60.21%)** with the sub-50% aspiration explicitly two-to-three years out and dependent on AI adoption plus income growth.
7. **No foreign branch** caps FCNR(B) participation to $20–25mn during an unusually attractive RBI window — a genuine franchise limitation until GIFT City opens.
8. **Recovery in written-off accounts is back-loaded** — Q1 delivered ₹80cr; management says "recovery happens more in the second half," so H1 other income stays soft.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Direct and self-aware. The MD did not hide behind the flat operating profit — he decomposed it (treasury ₹200cr → ₹80cr, lower TWO recovery) to show the core had improved, which is the correct and harder answer. He was equally blunt about the bank's legacy deficit and about not chasing FCNR(B) where the franchise cannot support it ("we don't have any big aspirations… because the ecosystem in our bank and geographical network doesn't facilitate that matter") — a refreshing refusal to over-promise into a fashionable window. He also **raised his own forward credit-growth view above the formal guidance** rather than sandbagging. The CFO answered net-worth composition to the rupee. Where the call is weaker: some gold-loan figures were quoted inconsistently between the MD and ED, and the ECL quantum remains undisclosed.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Flat operating profit is the bullish datapoint here, not the bearish one.** The bank replaced ~₹120cr of treasury gains and a chunk of written-off recovery with core NII and fee income, and still held the line. Earnings quality improved materially even though the headline didn't move.
- **The ₹5,000cr shedding is a hidden growth drag with a yield payoff.** Reported QoQ credit growth of 1.25% understates underlying origination because a large low-yield exposure was being run off simultaneously — and it was almost fully exited *after* 30 June, so Q2's optics improve mechanically.
- **The ₹123.5cr provisioning spike is an accounting choice, not a credit event.** ~₹150cr went to ECL pre-build; PCR rose to 92.33% as a direct consequence. Models treating this as rising credit cost will misread FY27 earnings.
- **Digital sourcing is already majority in two big retail products** — 62% of vehicle loans and 53% of home loans — with STP sanction rates of 40–50%. That is a far more advanced digital origination stack than the bank's size or reputation implies, and it is what makes the 64–65% RAM target credible.
- **The five-zone restructure and CENMARG consolidation** (from two zones to five, back-office sanctioning consolidated) is a Q1 structural change whose effect on TAT and credit quality will only show up over the coming quarters.
- **An analyst effectively wrote strategy on the call** — suggesting infrastructure bonds instead of FCNR(B) given the missing overseas branch — and the MD agreed they were already working on it. Watch for an infra-bond issue.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital adequacy well above regulatory floors at Jun'26: CRAR 17.61% (requirement 11.50%) on Rs. 14403 Cr capital, CET I including CCB 16.56% (requirement 8.00%) and Tier II only 1.05%; Risk Weighted Assets Rs. 81777 Cr.
- The deck reports no AT-1 capital (AT-1 row blank; Tier I equals CET I at Rs. 13541 Cr / 16.56% at Jun'26), so the Tier I stack is entirely common equity.
- Net Worth of Rs. 12500 Cr and Book Value Per Share of 17.62 at Jun'26 (Rs. 11315 Cr / 15.95 at Jun'25) on an unchanged share count of 709.56 crore shares and share capital of Rs. 7095.59 Cr - i.e. no equity issuance over the periods shown.
- Investment book positioned largely in HTM: of gross investments of Rs. 50866 Cr at Jun'26, HTM is Rs. 32773 Cr versus AFS + FVTPL (including HFT) Rs. 18093 Cr; SLR investments are 70.18% of the total, and GOI RECAP Bonds alone are 16.13%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **RAM is the strategic spine**: retail 25.82%, Agri 13.38%, MSME 20.82% of the book — 60.02% combined, targeting 64–65%.
- **Food and agro-processing** designated an internal "champion sector," delivering strong traction.
- **Digital STP journeys** live for KCC, education, personal, pre-owned vehicle and commercial vehicle loans, with ticket-size limits raised (**home loans up to ₹2cr; commercial vehicle and pre-owned up to ₹50 lakh**). **62% of vehicle loans and 53% of home loans are digitally sourced**; STP sanction rates ~40% in home loans and ~50% in vehicle loans. Digital loan-against-FD simplified; **loan against mutual funds next**.
- **Organisational restructure completed in Q1**: zonal offices expanded from **two to five**, with all regions under zones, and the **CENMARG back-office sanctioning structure consolidated into five zones** to improve quality and exploit regional opportunity.
- **Firsts/digital**: first public sector bank to offer **online PAN generation**; payment gateway live; **Bharat Connect Vista / Bharat Connect OMNI** salary products for central and state government employees.
- **Presence**: only ~450 districts covered — branch and BC expansion is a stated ongoing priority.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body: *Not a moat-rich franchise, and management does not claim one.* What was evidenced on the call is the **turnaround discipline** — RAM at 60% ahead of plan, PCR at 92.33%, ~82% of the non-NBFC corporate book at BBB+ or government-guaranteed, NBFC book ~92% AA/AAA, and a willingness to shed a ₹5,000cr low-yield relationship to protect NIM. The MD was candid about the starting point: "a bank which has its own legacy issues of no growth, no expansion, no capacity enhancement in HR and technology upgradation."
business.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Government of India holds 93.85% of the Bank, LIC 1.33% and Others 4.82% - unchanged across Jun'25, Mar'26 and Jun'26; Tier II Bonds and Infra Bonds are both rated 'AA (Stable)'.
- Deliberate tilt toward RAM: RAM advances at 60.02% of total advances as on Jun'26 (54.00% Jun'25, 58.80% Mar'26), with Corporate credit growth of only 3.73% YoY versus RAM growth of 32.66% YoY.
- Priority Sector Lending exceeds most mandated targets - Priority Sector 46.72% vs 40.00% mandate; Agriculture-PS 18.15% vs 18.00%; SMF 10.23% vs 10.00%; Weaker Section 12.05% vs 12.00%; Micro Enterprises 13.09% vs 7.50% - while Non Corporate Farmer at 12.17% is below the 14.00% mandate.
- Balance-sheet-light on unrated exposure: of credit rated above Rs. 5 Cr, 'Total of BBB & above' was 67.83% of total at Jun'26; within NBFC exposure 'Total A & above' was 99.76% at Jun'26.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [FY'27 Guidance] Deposit growth 13-14%, Advances growth 16-18%, RAM >60% of total advances, Gross NPA <2.0%, Net NPA <0.65%, PCR 92-93%, Recovery & Upgradation >Rs. 1000 Crore, Credit Cost (Annualised) <1% and Slippage Ratio (Annualised) <1%.
- [Guidance vs actual] Against those FY'27 targets the deck shows actuals as on Jun'26 of deposit growth 12.16%, advances growth 19.35% (above the 16-18% guided band), RAM 60.02%, GNPA 2.21%, NNPA 0.65%, PCR 92.33% and Recovery & Upgradation of 366 Crore.
- [Metric definition conflict] The deck states credit cost and slippage ratio two ways - the highlights page shows Credit Cost 0.11% and Slippage Ratio 0.18%, while the Guidance page shows 'Credit Cost (Annualised)' 0.43% and 'Slippage Ratio (Annualised)' 0.72% as actual on Jun'26.
- [Prior-period one-offs] The Key Financials series carries footnotes '* Including one-off item of Rs. 400 Crore' and '* Including one-off item of Rs. 255 Crore' against starred bars, so some historical quarters in those charts are not clean run-rate.
- [Award] Punjab & Sind Bank received the APY Annual Award of Excellence Achiever from PFRDA, presented by Secretary DFS Shri M Nagaraju, IAS, to MD & CEO Shri Swarup Kumar Saha.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- **NII +15.33%** is the quarter's core signal: the repo-rate reset drag has washed through, and yield-mix work (Agri, MSME, gold, mortgage, personal) is beginning to show. NIM 2.53% → guided 2.60–2.65%.
- **Yield strategy is explicitly a swap**: shed the ₹5,000cr low-yield government-guaranteed exposure; redeploy into higher-yielding RAM and selectively priced corporate.
- **Core fee income** is the second income leg: rationalised service charges, **system-driven charging**, and a new **Revenue Intelligence Wing** giving continuous feedback. Target ₹900–1,000cr for the year.
- **Cost-to-income at 60.21%** and structurally sticky: branch expansion, recruitment at all levels and technology investment are described as unavoidable costs of catching up. The route below 60% (and eventually below 50%) is income growth plus AI-driven process automation, not cost cuts.
- **Treasury is acknowledged as uncontrollable** — "you cannot wish away the fluctuations in the yield movement," with crude at ~$90 and the Gulf situation unresolved. India's index inclusion was expected to mitigate pressure.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1FY27 (this):** Business ₹2,66,420cr (+15.27%); advances +19.35% (retail +36%, Agri +25%+, MSME +32%) — **ahead of the 16–18% guidance**; deposits +12.16% (slightly below the 13–14% guide). RAM at 60.02%, targeting 64–65%. NII +15.33%; net profit ₹331cr (+23.05%); **operating profit flat at ₹545cr but on far lower treasury (₹80cr vs ~₹200cr LY) and lower TWO recovery — a quality improvement**. GNPA 2.21%, NNPA 0.65%, PCR 92.33%; slippages ₹207cr (0.18%); collection efficiency 95%; CRAR 17.61%; NIM 2.53%; C/I 60.21%; ROE 10.85%. **₹150cr of ECL pre-provisioning** drove the ₹123.5cr NPA provision. **₹5,000cr low-yield govt-guaranteed exposure ~50% shed by June, near-fully after.** Zonal offices 2→5 and CENMARG consolidated into five zones. Undisbursed sanctions ~₹15,000cr. FY29 plan: ₹4,00,000cr business, 2,000 branches, 6,000–6,500 BCs. GIFT City branch ~Nov-2026.
- _Q2FY27 → check: (a) sequential credit growth now that the ₹5,000cr run-off is complete — does it validate the 18–20% forward view; (b) NIM progression toward 2.60–2.65%; (c) RAM mix moving off 60.02% toward 64–65%; (d) MSME slippage run-rate and total SMA vs the sub-3% endeavour; (e) core fee income pacing to ₹900–1,000cr; (f) GIFT City branch opening in November; (g) any infrastructure-bond issuance; (h) launch of digital loan-against-mutual-funds, Digi Gold and CBDC; (i) the "new initiatives" management said would be disclosed after Q2._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Advances growth: guidance held at 16–18%, but management's forward view raised to "18% to 20% going forward"** and "19–20% growth is very much possible and is within our appetite."
- **Deposit growth: 13–14%** (Q1 came in slightly below at 12.16%).
- **RAM mix: from 60.02% to 64–65% by end of the year.**
- **NIM: 2.60–2.65%** (from 2.53%).
- **ROA: 0.85–0.90%.**
- **ROE: ~12%** (from 10.85%).
- **Cost-to-income: below 60%** this year; **below 50% aspirational in another two to three years.**
- **Core fee income target: ₹900–1,000cr for the current year.**
- **SMA 1+2: endeavour to bring total SMA below 3%.**
- **Net slippage: last year ₹677cr — "we would like not to breach that level, and hopefully… bring it down below ₹600 crores."**
- **Credit cost: guidance <1%**, deliberately conservative — "core credit cost should be very low, because we are not seeing any red flags anywhere in any sector"; the buffer is for ECL.
- **FCNR(B) + OFCB + ECB: ~$100mn total mobilisation expected**, of which FCNR(B) only **$20–25mn** — deliberately low ambition because the bank has no foreign branch to offer leveraging.
- **GIFT City branch: opening ~November 2026 (Q3 FY27)** — all approvals in place, team in place, only IT/technology work remaining.
- **Three-year plan: business of ₹4,00,000cr by FY29, with 2,000 branches, ~1,600 ATMs and 6,000–6,500 business correspondents.**
- **Gold loan: ~₹3,000cr of net increase during the year** (repayments are heavy monthly).
- **Loan against mutual funds — digital STP journey to launch "very shortly."** Digi Gold loans and **CBDC to be launched shortly.** Other new initiatives to be disclosed "maybe after the second quarter."
- 10-year G-sec: at 6.8% today, "6.90% is what we can touch very shortly."
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Undisbursed corporate sanctions of ~₹15,000cr** — the concrete near-term disbursement pipeline, with management stating they will be "very choosy on the pricing" and are "negotiating hard."
- Replacement strategy: the shed ₹5,000cr low-yield government-guaranteed exposure is to be **replaced with higher-yielding assets** across Agri, MSME, retail (gold, mortgage, personal) and selectively better-priced corporate.
- Housing: **141 projects already approved** for tie-up. Car loans: OEM tie-ups with **Maruti, Mahindra, Hyundai** plus other agencies.
- Co-lending: a **specialised co-lending cell**; gold and MSME co-lending to continue as priorities.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **GIFT City branch (Nov-2026)** — the bank's only route to overseas-style resource mobilisation and deployment; also the missing piece that currently caps FCNR(B) ambition.
- **Gold loans + co-lending** — the highest-yield retail lever, expanding both direct and through partners.
- **Loan against mutual funds (digital)**, CBDC, Digi Gold — near-term product launches.
- **Infrastructure bonds** — an analyst suggested this as a better-priced alternative to chasing FCNR(B) given no overseas branch; MD's response: "Yes, yes, you are right. We are working on that."
- **AI in systems and processes** — explicitly framed as the cost-to-income lever: routine work to business rule engines, redeploying staff into productive branch business.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality
